limitations_and_boundaries: The study does not directly demonstrate that bacterial SLs are the sole factor affecting host SL metabolism; other microbial metabolites may contribute.
The mouse models used (germfree, monocolonized, and conventionally raised) may not fully recapitulate human gut microbiome complexity.
The high-fat diet insulin resistance model uses a specific timeline and bacterial strain; generalizability to other diets or Bacteroides species is not established.
The transwell system does not replicate the full intestinal environment, including mucus layer and immune cells.
The study does not measure insulin sensitivity or glucose homeostasis directly in the BTWT vs SLMUT comparisons; only hepatic ceramide levels are reported.
The mechanism by which bacterial SLs inhibit host de novo synthesis (direct substrate competition vs. signaling) is not fully resolved.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.
